rows.selection_reason: With no prior evidence, the first experiment should establish a high-ceiling baseline using the most sophisticated components across all design axes: multimodal (both modalities), multiprofile (richer cellular context), scgpt (learned, biologically-informed RNA encoder), imagenet_vit_l (large pretrained image encoder), transformer aggregation (attention-based profile pooling), and weighted fusion (learned modality combination). This configuration tests whether the full pipeline can achieve strong validation accuracy and provides a reference upper bound. Subsequent experiments can then ablate individual components (e.g., swap scgpt→pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l→resnet50, transformer→avgpool) to identify which design choices drive performance, making this the most informative first probe under the 10-experiment budget.

We have only one data point (config_002: multimodal, pca_n2000 + imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted → 58.6% acc). The most critical uncertainty is whether multimodal fusion is actually adding value over a single modality. Config_013 (image_only, multiprofile, imagenet_vit_l, transformer) is the cleanest ablation of config_002: it removes the RNA modality while keeping the same image encoder and aggregation. If image-only approaches ~58%, the RNA branch isn't contributing and we should focus on image-centric or lighter multimodal configs; if it's substantially lower, the RNA signal is essential and we should explore RNA encoder variants (scgpt, scvi) and fusion strategies. Establishing this single-modality floor with 8 experiments remaining is the highest-information experiment before committing to a multimodal optimization trajectory.

Evidence: config_002 (multimodal, pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) achieves 0.586 accuracy, while image-only config_013 (same image encoder, transformer) achieves only 0.260, indicating RNA features are the dominant driver of performance. Question: config_002 uses PCA (a linear projection) for RNA; config_019 swaps in scgpt (a learned, non-linear RNA encoder) while keeping all other settings identical (imagenet_vit_l, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion, multiprofile). This isolates whether a more expressive RNA representation can push accuracy beyond 0.586. Why this is best: with 7 experiments remaining, testing the highest-impact single variable (RNA encoder quality, given RNA's clear dominance) around the current best configuration is the most informative exploitation step. A positive result would open a promising direction for further tuning; a null result would confirm PCA is sufficient and redirect effort toward other components (image encoder, fusion, aggregation).

Evidence: config_002 (pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) achieved the best accuracy (0.5856), and config_019 (scgpt, same other settings) scored lower (0.5200), confirming pca_n2000 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer is a strong backbone. Uncertainty: the fusion mechanism (weighted vs. concat) is the one component of this best config not yet varied in isolation. This experiment tests whether concat fusion can match or beat weighted fusion while keeping all other settings identical to the current best. It is the best use of experiment 4 because it is a single-variable exploitation of the top configuration, giving a clean, interpretable signal about fusion design before spending remaining budget on broader exploration (e.g., different image encoders or RNA encoders).

Evidence: The best config so far (config_038, acc=0.5988) uses pca_n2000 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + concat. We have shown pca_n2000 > scgpt (0.5856 vs 0.5199), but scvi_n200 remains completely untested. Question: Does the variational scvi_n200 RNA encoder outperform or match pca_n2000 under the best-known pipeline (imagenet_vit_l, transformer aggregation, concat fusion, multiprofile)? This is a clean single-variable change from the current best, isolating the RNA encoder effect. Why: With 5 experiments left, resolving the RNA encoder question is the highest-value uncertainty. If scvi_n200 is competitive, it opens a new optimization axis; if not, we can confidently lock in pca_n2000 and spend remaining budget fine-tuning aggregation/fusion or image encoder. This is the most informative next step before committing to exploitation of the current best.

Evidence: config_031 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, concat) achieved 0.7207 accuracy, far surpassing all other configs. The RNA encoder (scvi_n200) was the dominant factor, but the image encoder dimension has not yet been explored with scvi_n200. All top configs used imagenet_vit_l, and the image-only baseline (config_013) was very low (0.2596), suggesting the image branch contributes differently depending on the encoder. Question: Does resnet50 complement scvi_n200 better than imagenet_vit_l, potentially yielding a higher accuracy? This is the most impactful unexplored axis for our best-performing RNA encoder. Why this experiment: With 4 experiments remaining, testing a new image encoder paired with the clearly superior scvi_n200 + transformer + concat stack offers the highest potential upside to beat 0.7207, while keeping all other variables (aggregation, fusion, profile) fixed at their best-known values. It reduces uncertainty about whether the current 0.7207 is near-optimal or whether a different visual backbone could push performance higher.

The strongest evidence points to scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer as the optimal backbone (config_031: 0.7207 acc). The only untested dimension within this exact backbone is the fusion method: config_031 used concat, while weighted fusion remains untested with this combination. With pca_n2000, concat slightly outperformed weighted (0.5988 vs 0.5856), but the gap was small and scvi_n200 may interact differently with weighted fusion. Testing config_039 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted) is a minimal, high-information experiment: it either discovers a new best or confirms concat is optimal for the top backbone. With only 3 experiments remaining after this one, exploiting the strongest direction while resolving the last untested hyperparameter is the best use of the budget.

Evidence: The top two results (config_039: 0.7250, config_031: 0.7207) both use scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer, with weighted fusion marginally ahead of concat. All top performers use multiprofile and transformer aggregation. The only untested aggregation within this strongest encoder combination is avgpool. Question: Does avgpool aggregation with the scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + weighted fusion setup match or exceed the transformer-based result of 0.7250? Why this experiment: It is the single remaining untested variation in the most promising design space (best RNA encoder + best image encoder + best fusion), and with only 2 experiments left, testing the one unexplored axis (aggregation) within the proven top combination is the highest-information, highest-upside choice. If avgpool underperforms, it confirms transformer as optimal and we can confidently lock in config_039 as the final answer.

The current best is config_039 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted, acc=0.7250). The evidence strongly supports scvi_n200 as the RNA encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion. The key remaining uncertainty is whether the transformer+weighted advantage is specific to imagenet_vit_l or generalizable. Config_047 (scvi_n200 + resnet50 + transformer + weighted) is the only untested configuration that isolates the image encoder variable while holding the best aggregation and fusion fixed. It completes the critical 2x2 comparison for the top-performing architecture family. Even though resnet50 has underperformed vit_l in prior tests (0.6878 vs 0.7207 with concat), testing it with the stronger weighted fusion may reveal whether the gap narrows. This is the best use of the penultimate experiment because it either confirms imagenet_vit_l is essential (guiding the final experiment toward other untested dimensions) or reveals a competitive alternative, reducing uncertainty before the last experiment.

Evidence: The top-performing configurations consistently use scvi_n200 (RNA) + imagenet_vit_l (image) as encoders, with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion yielding the best result (config_039: 0.7250). Among untested configs, config_032 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + concat) is the only remaining multiprofile combination using both best-performing encoders. It tests whether the avgpool+concat pairing, while individually slightly weaker than transformer+weighted, might interact favorably with these strong encoders. This is the last experiment (0 remaining), so the goal is to maximize the probability of exceeding the current best of 0.7250. Config_032 has the highest expected accuracy among all untested options since it retains the two strongest encoders; all other untested scvi_n200 configs either swap to resnet50 (costing ~0.012) or use singleprofile (likely a larger drop). While the expected performance (~0.70-0.71) is unlikely to surpass 0.725, it is the best remaining bet to potentially improve the final result.
